name: triangle
title: Triangle
tagline: Single triangle from three vertices with angles, sides, ticks, right angles and altitude/cevians; colour-paired angle↔opposite-side annotation for sine/cosine/area-rule figures.
description: A single triangle drawn from three vertices, with any of its interior or exterior angles, side lengths, equal-side ticks and right angles marked, plus optional internal altitude / cevian lines dropped from a vertex to the opposite side. One figure for angles in a triangle (the interior angles add to 180°), isosceles and equilateral triangles, the exterior-angle theorem (extend a side), Pythagoras (right-angle mark + side lengths), trigonometry (SOHCAHTOA with opposite/adjacent/hypotenuse labels, the sine and cosine rules), and area (½ab·sinC, or ½·base·height using a dropped perpendicular). You place the vertices as a sketch in any units; the model derives every angle and side length from them and auto-fits the figure, so the marks stay correct. A cevian drops from a named vertex to the opposite side — a perpendicular altitude (the foot is the true projection, with a right-angle mark and a derived height) or a general line at a chosen fraction (a median at ½); the two sub-segments it splits the side into carry derived, label-overridable lengths. Per-element occlusion ("find x"), highlighting, a "not to scale" note and draggable vertices on the web. Override any displayed value with a label for the given data of a not-to-scale figure. For exam-style figures: vertexLabels: false suppresses the printed vertex letters while keeping A/B/C addressing; an angle with bare: true is marked with an arc and no value (so a derived measure cannot leak an answer); and a cevian entry can mark apexAngles — the sub-angle at its apex between the cevian line and one named side, with the arc terminating at the cevian. For the trig rules, pairs annotates the opposite-pair structure: each pair paints one angle mark and its partner side's length label in a shared hue (teal, then purple, then coral — one hue per pair, up to three), so the sine-rule ratio pairs (an angle with its opposite side), the cosine-rule pair, or the area-rule trio (the included angle with its two enclosing sides) are visible on the figure; the partner side derives as the side opposite the angle when not named. pairStrokes: true also draws the literal worked-solution stroke from each paired angle across to its opposite side — the hand-drawn gesture exam solutions use before writing the ratios.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the teaching lives on a triangle: the angle sum, isosceles/equilateral, the exterior-angle theorem, Pythagoras, SOHCAHTOA, the sine and cosine rules, the area rule, or any figure with a perpendicular height / dropped altitude. Place three vertices as [x, y] points making a sketch of the triangle (any units — [0,0],[6,0],[2,4]); the vertices default to labels A, B, C in the order given (override a vertex's label if you want different names). Reference an angle by its vertex label (at: "A") and a side by its two endpoint labels (between: ["A","B"]). The model derives each angle and side length from the vertices, so for a to-scale figure (e.g. a 3-4-5 Pythagoras triangle placed at [0,0],[4,0],[0,3]) just mark the element and the right number shows; for a not-to-scale exam figure place a rough sketch, set notToScale: true, and override each shown value with a label (the given data, e.g. "8 cm", "72°", "x"). Common configurations: angle sum — mark all three angles, give two and occlude+highlight the third. Isosceles — make two sides equal in the sketch, tick them, mark the equal base angles. Pythagoras — right-angle mark at the right-angled vertex, label the two known sides, occlude the unknown. SOHCAHTOA — right triangle, one acute angle given, label sides. Sine / cosine rule — any triangle, label the known sides and angles, occlude the unknown. Exterior angle — extend a side past a vertex and mark the exterior angle there; name the point the ray reaches with tipLabel on the extend entry (base A–B extended to C prints "C" at the tip, showing A, B, C collinear). ALTITUDE / PERPENDICULAR HEIGHT — add a cevians entry from the apex (cevians: [{ from: "A" }]); by default it is a perpendicular altitude, so the model drops the foot at the true projection onto the opposite side, draws a right-angle mark, and can show the derived height (label / occlude / showLength on the entry). Split the base into named pieces with segments: [{ toward: "B", label: "5 cm" }, { toward: "C" }] — each sub-segment length is derived (override with label on a not-to-scale figure). Name the foot with footLabel: "D". Mark a cevian EQUAL to a side with ticks (1–3, matching sides[].ticks): the isosceles-sub-triangle figure ticks side DA and cevian DB with one tick each to show DA = DB (a cevian to a base point splitting a triangle, the sub-triangle isosceles). For a NON-perpendicular line (a median or general cevian) set rightAngle: false and place it with at (0 at the opposite side's first vertex in your vertices order, 1 at the second; 0.5 = midpoint = median). Keep the sketch acute enough that a perpendicular foot lands within the side (external/obtuse feet are not drawn in v1). Occlude renders a value as "?"; the element itself stays drawn. EXAM FIGURES with no vertex letters — set vertexLabels: false; the letters stop printing but you still address angles/sides/cevians by the default A/B/C (or your custom labels). Mark an angle with an arc and NO value with bare: true on its angles entry — use it when the figure marks an angle without giving it (a derived or occluded value would change the question); occlude beats bare if both are set. Angle between a side and an altitude/cevian — never mark the whole vertex angle when the figure's arc stops at an internal line; instead put apexAngles on the cevians entry: apexAngles: [{ toward: "B", label: "65°" }] marks the angle at the cevian's apex between the apex→B side and the cevian line (toward names the opposite-side endpoint that side reaches; the measure is derived from the sketch, override with label on a not-to-scale figure; bare/occlude/highlight as on angles). Do not also mark the whole apex angle in angles[] — the two arcs would overlap. OPPOSITE-PAIR ANNOTATION (sine rule / cosine rule / area rule) — when the teaching move is "this angle pairs with this side", add pairs: each entry names an angle by its vertex label (pairs: [{ angle: "A" }, { angle: "C" }]) and the model paints that angle's arc + value AND its partner side's length label in one shared hue, a different hue per pair (teal, purple, coral by array position — keep the array order stable across the blocks/stages of a lesson so each pair keeps its hue). Omit sides to derive the partner as the side OPPOSITE the angle (the sine/cosine-rule pairing); for the area rule ½ab·sinC name the TWO enclosing sides explicitly (pairs: [{ angle: "C", sides: [["C","A"],["C","B"]] }]). Mark the paired angle in angles[] (label or bare) and give each paired side a sides[] entry (label or occlude) — the pair recolours those marks (a pair on an unmarked angle draws a bare arc in the hue; a paired side with no entry has no label to paint). highlight beats the pair hue — keep amber for the answer. Set pairStrokes: true to ALSO draw the hand-drawn worked-solution stroke from each paired angle across the triangle to its opposite side (the faithful exam-solution form; strokes only draw to a side opposite the angle, never to one touching its vertex). Stage the pairs one beat at a time by growing the array (stage 1: pairs: [pair1]; stage 2: [pair1, pair2]) with the matching ratio in each beat's text. Cross-block convention: keep the same triangle shape and vertex labels across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track the triangle, not a redrawn sketch — change only what is given, occluded or highlighted. Almost any triangle figure can be built up in stages (empty triangle → add the givens → drop the altitude → reveal the answer). UNITS — set unit: "cm" once per figure to append it to every bare-number length label (derived or authored "12"); a label carrying its own text ("12 cm", "x") stays verbatim. Synonyms a teacher might use: triangle, angles in a triangle, angle sum, isosceles, equilateral, scalene, base angles, exterior angle, missing angle, Pythagoras, hypotenuse, right-angled, SOHCAHTOA, trigonometry, sine rule, cosine rule, opposite, adjacent, area of a triangle, perpendicular height, altitude, drop a perpendicular, foot of the perpendicular, cevian, median, not to scale, opposite pairs, pair the angle with its opposite side, included angle, colour-coded ratios.

vertices.description: The three corners of the triangle, in order. Each is a point in any units — place them as a SKETCH of the triangle you want; the model derives the angles and side lengths from them and auto-fits the figure to the canvas. The order fixes the default labels: the first corner is A, the second B, the third C. Avoid a degenerate (near-collinear) triangle.

at.description: Position of this corner as [x, y] in your own units (y up). Only the SHAPE matters — the figure is scaled to fit.

label.description: Display name for this corner, drawn just outside it. Defaults to A, B, C by order. Override for different names (and then reference this corner by the new label in angles/sides/extend/cevians).

angles.description: The angles to MARK with an arc and a value. Address each by its vertex label (the default A/B/C, or a custom label). The measure is DERIVED from the vertices; for a not-to-scale figure override it with label. Omit a vertex to leave its angle unmarked.

at.description: Which vertex this angle sits at — the vertex label (e.g. "A").

label.description: Override the displayed value — the given measure on a not-to-scale figure ("72°"), or an unknown ("x"). Omit to show the measure derived from the vertices (e.g. "59°").

occlude.description: Render this angle's value as "?" — the "find the missing angle" hook. The arc still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this angle (amber arc + value) — the answer, or the angle a question is about. Default false.

bare.description: Mark this angle with the arc ONLY — no value text. Use when the source figure marks an angle without giving its size (printing the derived measure would leak an answer). occlude beats bare: set occlude instead when the question asks FOR this angle. Default false.

rightAngle.description: Mark this angle as a right angle: a small square instead of an arc and value. Use when the vertex is the right angle of the triangle. Default false.

exterior.description: Mark the EXTERIOR angle at this vertex (between an extended side and the next side) instead of the interior one. Requires a matching extend entry through this vertex. Use for the exterior-angle theorem. Default false.

sides.description: The sides to LABEL with a length and/or tick as equal. Address each by its two endpoint vertex labels. The length is DERIVED from the vertices; override with label for the given value or an unknown. Omit a side to leave it bare.

between.description: The two endpoint vertex labels of this side, e.g. ["A","B"] (order does not matter).

label.description: Override the displayed length — the given value ("8 cm", "x"), or a trig role ("opposite", "adjacent", "hypotenuse"). Omit to show the length derived from the vertices.

occlude.description: Render this side's length as "?" — the "find the missing side" hook. The side stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this side (amber) — the answer, or the side in question. Default false.

ticks.description: Draw this many small equal-length ticks across the side. Sides with the SAME tick count read as equal (isosceles = 1 tick on each of the two equal sides; congruence figures use 1, 2, 3 to pair sides). Omit for no tick.

cevians.description: Internal lines dropped from a vertex to a point on the opposite side — an altitude (perpendicular height), a median, or a general cevian. Each splits the opposite side into two sub-segments whose lengths are derived (override with a label on a not-to-scale figure). Usually one. Omit for none. @2.

from.description: The vertex label the line drops FROM (its apex). The line lands on the opposite side — the one not touching this vertex.

rightAngle.description: Whether this is a perpendicular altitude. Default TRUE: the foot is placed at the true perpendicular projection of the apex onto the opposite side and a right-angle square is drawn there, so the mark is always a genuine 90° even on a not-to-scale sketch (`at` is ignored). Set false for an oblique line (median / general cevian) placed by `at`, with no square.

at.description: For an oblique cevian (rightAngle: false) only: the foot's fractional position along the opposite side, 0 at the side's first endpoint in your vertices order and 1 at the second. 0.5 = the midpoint (a median). Ignored for a perpendicular altitude (its foot is derived). Default 0.5.

footLabel.description: Optional name for the foot point where the line meets the side (e.g. "D"), drawn just outside the side at the foot. Omit for no name.

ticks.description: Draw this many equal-length ticks across the cevian line, so it can be marked EQUAL to a ticked side. A cevian and a side carrying the SAME tick count read as equal — the isosceles-sub-triangle figure: tick side DA and cevian DB with one tick each to show DA = DB. Matches sides[].ticks (same accent tick). Omit for no tick. @6.

label.description: Override the displayed length of the cevian itself (the perpendicular height) — a given value ("h", "12 cm") or an unknown ("x"). Omit to leave the line unlabelled unless showLength is set.

occlude.description: Render the cevian's own length as "?" (the "find the height" hook) and draw its length position. The line still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to the cevian line and its length (amber) — the answer, or the height a question is about. Default false.

showLength.description: Show the derived length of the cevian (the perpendicular height) even with no label. Default false — a bare cevian draws just the line. (label or occlude also force the length to show.)

apexAngles.description: Mark the sub-angle(s) at this cevian's APEX between the cevian line and one of the apex's two sides — the arc terminates at the cevian. Use when a figure marks the angle between a side and an internal altitude (a whole-vertex angles entry would sweep across the cevian and read as the full apex angle). At most one per side. Omit for none. @3.

toward.description: Which side of the apex bounds this sub-angle: the opposite-side endpoint that side reaches (a vertex label, e.g. "B" marks the angle between side apex→B and the cevian).

label.description: Override the displayed value — the given measure on a not-to-scale figure ("65°") or an unknown ("x°"). Omit to show the measure derived from the sketch.

occlude.description: Render this sub-angle's value as "?" — the "find this angle" hook. The arc still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this sub-angle (amber arc + value). Default false.

bare.description: Arc only, no value text (as angles[].bare). occlude beats bare. Default false.

segments.description: Label the two sub-segments the foot splits the opposite side into. Each length is DERIVED; override with label. Address a sub-segment by the endpoint it reaches (toward). Omit for unlabelled sub-segments.

toward.description: The opposite-side endpoint this sub-segment reaches — a vertex label. The sub-segment runs from the foot to this vertex (e.g. toward: "B" is the foot→B piece).

label.description: Override the displayed length of this sub-segment — the given value ("5 cm", "x"). Omit to show the length derived from the vertices.

occlude.description: Render this sub-segment's length as "?" — the "find this piece" hook. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this sub-segment (amber). Default false.

extend.description: Side extensions, for exterior-angle figures. Each draws the side from one vertex through another and onward past it as a ray, so the exterior angle at the far vertex can be marked (an angles entry there with exterior: true). Omit for none.

from.description: The vertex label the side starts at.

through.description: The vertex label the side passes through; the ray continues past this vertex. The exterior angle is marked here.

tipLabel.description: Optional letter drawn at the FAR tip of the extended ray — the collinear point beyond `through` (e.g. base A–B extended to C prints "C" at the ray end, so "A, B and C lie on a straight line" is shown on the figure). Use when the source figure names the point the side is extended to. Omit for an unnamed ray. @6.

pairs.description: Opposite-pair annotation — the sine/cosine/area-rule teaching move of visually pairing an angle with its partner side(s). Each pair paints one marked angle (arc + value) and its partner side's length label in one shared hue, a DISTINCT hue per pair (teal, then purple, then coral — array position fixes the hue, so keep the order stable across the blocks/stages of a lesson). Mark the paired angle in angles[] (a pair on an unmarked angle draws a bare arc in the hue) and give each partner side a sides[] entry so there is a label to paint. highlight on an element beats its pair hue (amber stays the answer); when two pairs claim one side, the first keeps it. Omit for none. @4.

angle.description: The vertex label of the paired angle (e.g. "A"). Interior angles only.

sides.description: The partner side(s), each as its two endpoint vertex labels (e.g. [["B","C"]]; order within a side does not matter). OMIT to derive the side OPPOSITE the angle — the sine/cosine-rule partner. For the area rule ½ab·sinC name the TWO sides enclosing the included angle explicitly (e.g. angle "C" with sides [["C","A"],["C","B"]]).

items.description: One side, as its two endpoint vertex labels.

pairStrokes.description: With pairs: also draw the literal worked-solution stroke from each paired angle across the triangle to its partner side (a straight line in the pair hue, stopped short of the side) — the hand-drawn gesture exam solutions use before writing the sine-rule ratios. Strokes only draw to a side OPPOSITE the angle (never to a side touching its vertex — colour alone carries an area-rule pair). Default false. @4.

unit.description: The figure's length unit, e.g. "cm", "m", "mm". Appended to every length label that is a BARE NUMBER — a derived length or a purely numeric authored label ("12" → "12 cm"). A label with any other text ("12 cm", "x", "2x + 1") is shown verbatim — an authored override always wins. Angle labels never take it. Default "" (labels stay bare). Set it once per figure and keep it consistent across a lesson. @5.

vertexLabels.description: Whether to PRINT the vertex letters beside the corners. Set false for exam figures drawn without letters (common in sine/cosine-rule questions) — addressing in angles/sides/extend/cevians still uses the default A/B/C (or custom labels); only the printing is suppressed. Default true.

notToScale.description: Print a "Not to scale" note by the figure. Only when the source figure prints one — most exam figures don't. Default false.

caption.description: An optional line of text centred below the figure — the rule or fact being taught, e.g. "Angles in a triangle add to 180°" or "Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal". Omit for none.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

draggablePoints.description: Web-only. Let pupils drag a vertex to reshape the triangle; the derived angles, side lengths and any cevian foot/height recompute live while the angle sum stays 180° — the invariant. Best on a to-scale figure (no overridden labels). Default false.
